info.title: API.SH: Udemy
info.description: The Udemy API from API.SH: public Udemy data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

200.description: The stored response (headers: x-refetch: 1, x-original-time, x-original-route).

404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

get.description:
Udemy's categories, each with its subcategories (id, title, link). With `subcategory_id`, that subcategory's popular topics instead (id, title, link); topic ids work as `topic_id` in search and as `id` with `type=topic` in /udemy/v1/category.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/udemy-categories

parameters.name: subcategory_id
parameters.description: A subcategory id, e.g. `8`, to list its topics.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Topics to list with subcategory_id (default 30, max 100).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Udemy courses in a category or topic
get.description:
The courses of a Udemy category, subcategory or topic page, 16 per page, with the same filters and course fields as search, plus `filter_options`. Pass a numeric id with `type` (ids from /udemy/v1/categories, topic ids from search filters) or the page's link (udemy.com/courses/development/web-development/ or udemy.com/topic/python/). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/udemy-category

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A category, subcategory or topic id (e.g. `8`, Web Development), or a udemy.com/courses/... or /topic/... link.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: What the numeric id is (default `subcategory`); not needed with a link.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order: `relevance` (default for search), `most_reviewed` (default for categories), `highest_rated`, `newest`.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Comma-separated levels: `all`, `beginner`, `intermediate`, `expert`.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Comma-separated video lengths: `extra_short` (0-1 h), `short` (1-3 h), `medium` (3-6 h), `long` (6-17 h), `extra_long` (17 h+).

parameters.name: price
parameters.description: `free`, `paid`, or both comma-separated.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Comma-separated two-letter course languages, e.g. `en,es`.

parameters.name: subtitles
parameters.description: Comma-separated two-letter subtitle languages, e.g. `en`.

parameters.name: min_rating
parameters.description: Minimum average rating: 3, 3.5, 4 or 4.5.

parameters.name: topic_id
parameters.description: Comma-separated topic ids (the `courseLabel` values in `filter_options`, e.g. 7380 for Python).

parameters.name: features
parameters.description: Comma-separated hands-on features the course must have: `quizzes`, `coding_exercises`, `practice_tests`, `role_plays`.

parameters.name: certification_prep
parameters.description: `true`: certification prep courses only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1). Pass `next_page` back; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

A course's landing page data: id, slug, title, headline, full description (text and HTML), list price, current discount price and percent, average and recent rating, review counts, rating distribution by stars, students, instructors, level, language, caption languages, category, subcategory and topics, badges, total length, lectures, quizzes, practice tests, coding exercises, articles, downloadable resources, certificate, requirements, what you'll learn, who it is for, FAQ, created / published / last updated dates, image and preview link. `raw` keeps the site's full record.

get.description:
A course's student reviews, 20 per page, most relevant first as on the course page (or newest first): rating, text, date, reviewer name and avatar, and the instructor's response when there is one; plus the total. Filter by star rating with `rating`; `text_only=false` also lists ratings left without a comment. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/udemy-reviews

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Course slug, numeric id, or a udemy.com/course/... link.

parameters.name: rating
parameters.description: Only reviews with this many stars (1 to 5).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order (default `relevant`).

parameters.name: text_only
parameters.description: Default true: only reviews with a written comment.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1). Pass `next_page` back; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Courses matching a search, 24 per page, with every filter of Udemy's search page: id, title, headline, link, average rating and review count, level, language, last update, video length, lecture count, free flag, badges (Bestseller, Highest Rated...), instructors, image, what you'll learn, lectures that matched the search. Also the total, page count, a did-you-mean suggestion and `filter_options` (every filter with its values and course counts, as the site shows them). Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/udemy-search

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
